name: Southeast Slope (Standard Route)
approach: From the Thirtymile Trailhead (end of FR 5160, ~3,400 ft) or the Andrews Creek Trailhead (end of FR 51, ~3,050 ft), hike into the Pasayten Wilderness. Via Thirtymile: follow the Chewuch River Trail and Four Point Creek Trail to Four Point Lake (6,850 ft), then pick up the abandoned Coleman Ridge Trail; at roughly 7,070 ft a cairn marks the point to leave the trail and climb open meadow/talus up-valley to the summit on a well-trodden unofficial path. Via Andrews Creek: hike the Andrews Creek Trail roughly 9-11 miles (crossing heavy deadfall in an old 2003 burn in the lower miles) to a low saddle between Remmel and Coleman Ridge, then contour the west side of Coleman Ridge to reach the same upper slopes; alternatively continue to Andrews Pass (~6,700 ft) and climb one of several Class 3 west-facing gullies directly to the summit ridge.

road.name: West Chewuch Road (County Rd 1213) to Forest Road 51 / FR 5160
road.status: Improved gravel Forest Service road; high-clearance recommended near the trailheads, especially early season
road.driveNote: From Winthrop, drive north on West Chewuch Road (County Rd 1213) about 6 miles to where it becomes Forest Road 51; continue roughly 22 miles to the Andrews Creek Trailhead at road's end, or fork onto FR 5160 near mile 20 and continue about 11 miles total to the Thirtymile Trailhead.
